newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Cargill food export a lifeline for N. Korea.
newsitem.headline: Cargill food export a lifeline for N. Korea.

text.p: A licence for U.S. trading giant Cargill Inc to export food to North Korea will provide a sorely-needed lifeline to the communist state, a South Korean analyst said on Tuesday.
"North Korea will face a food shortage from the end of April this year when their food supplies are expected to run out," said Kim Woon-keun, research director of the Korea Rural Economic Institute.
Analysts in Seoul said the food shipment by Cargill to North Korea would probably be completed by late April.

North Korea has suffered two years of flooding that depleted food supplies and left people severely short of food. The United States gave US$2 million in February 1996 to alleviate the near-famine conditions.

Buying all the grain authorised by the Cargill licence could easily cost $100 million, based on U.S. prices and shipping costs. U.S. grain analysts said high U.S. prices might force Cargill to fill an order with grain from other nations.
North Korea has been in a negotiations with Cargill since mid-1996 over supplies of rice and wheat, a South Korean government official said.

On Monday, the U.S. Treasury gave the Minneapolis firm permission to export 500,000 tonnes of wheat and rice to North Korea, a week after the communist nation apologised for a submarine incursion into South Korean waters.
Cargill said it applied last September for the licence.

Some trade sources were sceptical a deal would be struck with Pyongyang, which was believed to have little money for direct food purchases. Barters are difficult to arrange and can be risky financially, they said.
While Cargill said its licence was issued on December 30, the day after North Korea apologised, U.S. officials did not confirm the approval until Monday.
A government source, who declined to be named, said contacts between the two seemed to have started in New York and there may have been a third party involved in the negotiations.
Speculation has centred on Japan, South Korea and Taiwan as possible third parties. The government source declined to comment on this but he ruled out South Korea.
